notes:
Context: Oakmont is a mid-to-large financial data provider building a conversational support agent + document search for compliance staff. They have strict data residency and audit needs; leaning toward Redwood Dedicated (VPC) with potential Private on-prem later. Primary negotiation focus: deterministic latency SLOs for SLAs, predictable reserved GPU planning, and clear measurement methodology for streaming vs non-streaming workloads.

Key latency SLO discussion points (CRM-style fragments / call notes):
- Customer wants explicit p50/p95/p99 SLOs by request type (chat short-turn vs long-form summarization vs embeddings search). Example targets discussed: non-streaming text gen p95 < 200ms (short prompts, 256 tokens max), p99 < 500ms; streaming chat TTFB p95 < 150ms, incremental chunk p95 < 50ms. These are starting points; negotiable with tradeoffs.
- Measurement alignment: Oakmont insists on "end-to-end" timing in SLA: client-side observed latency (ingress->response complete). Redwood prefers server-side infer-time + network RTT breakdown. Agreed approach: report both client-side (application ingress timestamp) and normalized server-side (ingest->last-token-emitted) with documented clock sync assumptions.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: define two buckets in contract. Streaming SLOs measured as time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and steady-state per-chunk latency; non-streaming measured as time-to-last-byte (TTLB). Also record time-to-first-token for latent models. If streaming transport uses HTTP/2 chunking or websocket, measurement hooks must capture per-chunk emit timestamps.
- P50/P95/P99 semantics: define percentiles over successful (200) responses only; timeouts and server errors are counted as SLA violations in availability metric, not in latency percentiles. Must specify sample window (rolling 30d) and minimum sample size for percentile validity (suggested min 10k samples/day or explicit fallback rules).
- Warm vs cold starts & caching: agreed to exclude cold-container startup (scale-up) events from latency SLOs if they occur during autoscale > configured burst window. KV/prefix cache hits should be tagged; metrics must include cache-hit vs miss breakdown so Oakmont can correlate p99 spikes to cold cache.
- Client-side timing normalization: require NTP-synced clocks or use request-id correlation where client attaches a monotonic client-timestamp header; Redwood will validate with server-received timestamp to compute network vs infer components.
- Throughput guarantees and reserved GPU planning: reviewed capacity formula during workshop. Example calc: target 200 sustained QPS for short-chat profile -> estimate 4 A10G-like GPUs reserved with conservative concurrency 8 and batching window 20ms; batch sizing and quantization profiles to be tuned by Redwood Optimize team to hit p95 targets. Discussed burst buffer policy and pre-warmed instances to limit scale-up latency.
- SLA negotiations: Oakmont requests credits tied to p95 breaches > 3 days in a 30d window. Redwood proposes graduated credits with rollbacks for repeated incidents and a mutual time-to-resolution SLA (incident response / RCA cadence). Also proposed automatic fallback routing to a compatible lower-capacity model variant if primary capacity constrained; Oakmont wants opt-in for potential quality regression.
- Observability: Oakmont requires per-request trace IDs, token-level timing, and histogram exports (p50/p95/p99) to their Prometheus/Datadog. Also asked for retention of detailed logs for 90 days for audits.

Actionable next steps (from AE/SE notes):
- Run 3-day synthetic load test on Redwood Dedicated mirror with Oakmont workload replay (Sofia to own test run, target window 2026-03-15 -> 2026-03-17). Collect client-side and server-side traces.
- Deliver a capacity plan mapping target QPS to reserved GPU count, with alternative configs (quantized model, larger batch, lower concurrency) and estimated token/sec per-GPU.
- Draft SLA termsheet with explicit definitions: measurement points, percentile windows, error handling, credit bands, and streaming vs non-streaming buckets. Legal to review.
- Confirm telemetry integration method (trace-id header format, metrics endpoints) and provide sample dashboard templates.
